name: Village on Eastbrook
award: 2025 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Housing Catalyst, the Fort Collins housing authority, is building Village on Eastbrook, a three-story, all-electric building with 73 one- and two-bedroom apartments for households at 30% to 80% AMI (average 57.5%) at 3221 Eastbrook Drive in southeast Fort Collins. It won 2025 Round Two federal 4% and accelerated state credits from CHFA.
why_it_matters: It shows a housing authority using Prop 123 land banking money to buy a fully entitled site, issuing its own bonds on a general revenue pledge, and swapping city CDBG/HOME money for local capital tax dollars to avoid Build America, Buy America costs. The deal closed in spring 2026 and broke ground on 2026-06-09.

status.label: Under construction; financing closed spring 2026, groundbreaking 2026-06-09
status.detail: Fort Collins Affordable Housing Board minutes of 2026-05-07 record that Housing Catalyst had closed on the project the week before and was in construction. Housing Catalyst held a groundbreaking on 2026-06-09, posted monthly construction updates through September 2026, and expects completion in summer 2027, with applications from February 2027 and move-ins from June 2027 (subject to change).

next_step: Watch Housing Catalyst's construction updates and leasing page for the February 2027 application opening, then a certificate of occupancy and CHFA 8609 in 2027.

key_numbers.meaning: 44 one-bedroom and 29 two-bedroom units at 30% to 80% AMI under income averaging, average 57.5% AMI.
Plus $1,800,000 in accelerated state credit and $17,920,000 in private activity bonds, per CHFA's award report.
$478,500 per unit, per Housing Catalyst's December 2025 request to the city. Hard costs were estimated at $20,426,145 including solar.
One of the first 16 state land banking awards (January 2024); it paid for the land of a site sold with full entitlements and plans.

facts.value: 2.9 acres of vacant land, about 25 units per acre; not in a QCT; one block west of Fort Collins High School and next to the Power Trail
One three-story, L-shaped, wood-frame (Type VB) building with two elevators; all units Type A accessible or Type B adaptable

All-electric with a 333 kW rooftop and carport solar array expected to offset about 70% of building energy use; Enterprise Green Communities and ENERGY STAR Multifamily New Construction; 8 EV-ready spaces
All units to be certified under Colorado State University's Institute for the Built Environment Lifelong Homes Pilot Certification
Bus routes 11 and 12 within half a mile were suspended at application; free on-demand taxi service runs during bus hours
Single electric meter; Housing Catalyst pays all utilities and provides free Wi-Fi through Fort Collins Connexion
Housing Catalyst issues the bonds itself as a public offering with a general revenue pledge (S&P AA- rating), using volume cap from the City of Fort Collins and Larimer County
None; the applicant removed all PBVs because of federal funding uncertainty

background.text: A local developer offered Housing Catalyst the 2.9-acre vacant parcel with architectural plans, permits and approvals for a fully entitled apartment building. Prop 123 land banking money paid for the land portion of the purchase, and Housing Catalyst bought the site in 2024.

The project went through city development review under the earlier owner: a virtual neighborhood meeting on 2022-08-22, and unanimous Planning and Zoning Commission approval on 2022-12-14, per the applicant. The Final Development Plan and Development Agreement were approved by 2025.

Housing Catalyst first sought a 4% federal and state credit award in August 2024. It said two competitive tax credit applications were needed, which pushed the construction start from spring 2025 to spring 2026.

Early plans capped average income at 60% AMI, with all units at or below 60% AMI and up to 25 project-based vouchers. The awarded plan uses income averaging from 30% to 80% AMI (average 57.5%) with no PBVs.

Housing Catalyst asked the city in December 2025 to swap its $1.2M CDBG/HOME award for local capital tax money, saying Build America, Buy America compliance would add $700,000 to $1.7M in costs. The total city subsidy stays at $1.5M, about $20,500 per unit.

The market study (June 2025) found 3.1% overall vacancy in the primary market area, 0.9% at Class B LIHTC properties and 0.0% at senior LIHTC properties. The nearest tax credit property is Fox Meadows Apartments, about 0.7 mile away. The analyst noted a nearby active railway; the design adds noise attenuation.

The budget includes a 1% Build America, Buy America contingency and a 1.5% tariff contingency. Construction was planned to take about 12 months because utilities, curb, gutter, sidewalk and driveway were already in place.
The 2024 city application described a 40-year LIHTC affordability restriction, plus city and Division of Housing use restrictions of about 15 or 20 years.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award report lists $17,920,000 in bonds, while the application narrative puts total tax-exempt bonds at $17,320,000 (plus $7,000,000 of short-term taxable bonds).
The application narrative describes a $2.2 million Housing Catalyst carryback note for the land, while the December 2025 sources table shows a $0.8 million seller carry.
Housing Catalyst and the state announced a $1,610,000 Prop 123 land banking award, while the December 2025 sources table shows $1.3 million from that source.
Housing Catalyst's November 2025 award announcement expected completion in spring 2027, while its project and leasing pages say summer 2027.
